question: Who was the 1st Indian woman to preside over Indian National Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarojini Naidu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sarojini Naidu** was the first Indian woman to preside over the Indian National Congress.
 
• She was elected as the president of the Congress session in **1925** at Kanpur.
 
• Sarojini Naidu is also known as the **"Nightingale of India"** due to her contributions to poetry.
 
• She played a significant role in India's struggle for independence and was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi's ideas of non-violence and civil disobedience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

 
 
• Founded in 1885, the Indian National Congress is one of the two major political parties in India.
 
• It played a crucial role in the Indian independence movement against British rule.
 
• The INC was the party of prominent leaders like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel, who led the country to independence in 1947.
 
• Post-independence, the INC became the dominant political party in India for several decades.
 
 
 
• **Role of Women in Indian National Congress**
 
 
• Women played a significant role in the Indian independence movement and in the Indian National Congress.
 
• Leaders like Sarojini Naidu, Annie Besant, and Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit were pioneers in advocating for women's rights and participation in politics.
 
• The involvement of women in the INC helped in mobilizing a large section of society for the cause of independence.
 
• Post-independence, women leaders continued to play important roles in Indian politics and governance.
 
 
 
• **Sarojini Naidu's Contributions**
 
 
• Sarojini Naidu was not only a political leader but also a celebrated poet.
 
• Her poetry includes themes of love, nature, and Indian patriotism. She was a part of the Indian Renaissance movement.
 
• Naidu was also involved in social work, focusing on issues like women's empowerment, education, and healthcare.
 
• She was appointed the first woman Governor of an Indian state (United Provinces, now Uttar Pradesh) after independence.
